viral_post.text: Finance Minister Petra Lund on pensions: 'Pensioners have had it too good for too long.' Unbelievable. RT if you're a pensioner and angry.

assembly_record.sitting: Norland Assembly (fictional), Second Reading debate, Pensions Indexation (Amendment) Bill
assembly_record.text: THE SPEAKER: I call the Minister of Finance to open the debate. MINISTER LUND: Thank you, Speaker. This bill changes how pensions are uprated each year. At present, every pension rises by the higher of prices or wages. Under this bill, the basic pension and the pension credit will continue to rise by the higher of the two, and the top-up earnings-related pension will rise by prices only. I want to be clear with the House, because I know what will be said about this: I have never said, and I would never say, that pensioners have had it too good. The lowest pensions are protected in full by this bill. MR. GARRICK HALE (Opposition): The minister's position seems to be that pensioners have had it too good for too long. That is what this bill says to every pensioner who worked forty years to earn that top-up. She can dress it up however she likes. MINISTER LUND: The honourable member is putting words in my mouth, and he knows it. MS. INGRID SOLVANG: On a point of order, Speaker, the member for Eastmark South has been waiting since the last sitting for an answer on the ferry subsidy. THE SPEAKER: That is not a point of order, but the minister for transport will have heard it. MR. TOBIAS ERNE: I rise to speak about the effect on widows' pensions, which the committee did not examine. The inherited portion of the top-up pension is often the only income a widow has beyond the basic pension. I will be tabling an amendment in committee. MINISTER LUND: I will look carefully at any amendment on inherited entitlements. MR. HALE: We'll hold her to that. MS. SOLVANG: Speaker, may I ask the minister whether the fiscal council has published its costing of the change? MINISTER LUND: It will publish before committee stage. THE SPEAKER: Order. The question is that the bill be now read a second time. Division called. The ayes have it.

state.headline: Court Strikes Down City's Rent Cap
state.body: The state Court of Appeal on Friday struck down one provision of Ellisport's rent stabilisation ordinance, ruling that the city exceeded its authority when it applied the annual cap to single-family homes owned by individual landlords with two or fewer properties. The court left the rest of the ordinance in place, including the 4 percent annual cap on apartment buildings, which cover the large majority of the city's rental units. 'The cap stands for nearly every renter in Ellisport,' said city attorney Rosa Imbert. The landlords' association, which brought the case, called the ruling 'a partial victory' and said it was considering an appeal to the state Supreme Court on the remaining provisions. The ruling applied the ordinance's severability clause, which says that if any part is held invalid the remainder continues in effect. Tenant advocates said they would ask the council to explore other ways to protect renters in single-family homes. In a separate matter, the court declined to hear a challenge to the city's short-term rental registry.
state.ruling_excerpt: Section 5(c), to the extent it applies to single-family dwellings owned by natural persons holding no more than two rental properties, is invalid. Pursuant to Section 14 (severability), the remaining provisions of the ordinance are unaffected. The trial court's judgment is otherwise affirmed. Each party shall bear its own costs on appeal.
state.ordinance_s14: Section 14. Severability. If any provision of this ordinance or its application to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect other provisions or applications that can be given effect without the invalid provision or application.
social_reaction: Landlord forum: 'RENT CAP IS DEAD. Raise away.'
Tenant union: 'Read the ruling. Your cap still applies unless you rent a house from a small landlord.'
City council member post: 'Staff will brief council next week on what this means for single-family renters.'
state.city_faq: Q: My apartment building has 12 units. Does the cap still apply? A: Yes. The ruling does not affect apartment buildings. Q: I rent a house from someone who owns only that house. A: The cap may no longer apply to you. Contact the rent board before accepting an increase above 4 percent; other protections, such as notice periods, still apply.
state.rent_board_note: The rent board said it had received more than two hundred calls since the ruling, most from apartment tenants whose landlords had cited the headline when proposing increases above the cap. The board reminded landlords that increases above 4 percent on covered apartments remain unlawful and can be challenged.

claim.text: The Drennan River salmon run is the lowest ever recorded. The fisheries ministry admits it.

sources.text: Preliminary counts at the Drennan River fish fence indicate a return well below the ten-year average. Final counts will be published after the season closes. Preliminary counts are routinely revised, sometimes substantially, when fence data are reconciled with spawning-ground surveys. Commercial openings on the lower river remain closed; the recreational fishery is limited to catch-and-release above the Tallis Bridge.

Our volunteers' spawning-ground walks this autumn found fewer redds than in any year since we began surveying in 2004. The Society's survey covers the upper tributaries only. We thank the forty-two volunteers who walked the Kessel, Ammon and Little Drennan creeks, often in heavy rain, and remind members that the annual meeting is on the first Saturday of next month.

A ministry biologist, speaking on condition of anonymity because she was not authorised to comment, said the run 'might be the worst on record, but we won't know until the count is final'. The ministry's official record-keeping for the Drennan began in 1962. Several guides told the paper they had seen fewer fish than in any season they could remember, though none had kept counts. A spokesperson for the fishing lodge association said bookings had fallen by a third.
The lowest final count in the ministry's Drennan series occurred in 1994. This table will be updated when the current season's final count is published.

sources.source: ministry press office reply to the desk
sources.text: The ministry has not described this year's run as a record. Any statement about records will follow publication of the final count.

The Drennan Valley Guides' Association said its members had logged far fewer fish per trip this season than in any recent year, based on the voluntary catch cards members fill in after each trip. The association acknowledged that catch cards are not a scientific count, that effort varies with river conditions, and that several members fished less because of the catch-and-release rules. It called on the ministry to publish the final count promptly and to fund a second fish fence on the Kessel tributary.

state.reader_context: The claim was posted before the season closed.

verdict.note: Counts are preliminary and routinely revised; the ministry table still shows 1994 as the low and awaits the final count; the Society's record is partial and shorter. Nothing settles 'lowest ever' yet.

official_record.text: CHAIR BAIRD: We'll continue with the subsidy review. Senator Okonjo, you have the floor. SENATOR OKONJO: Thank you, Chair. I've heard people say farm subsidies are welfare for the rich and should be abolished. I don't agree with that. Family farms in my state would not survive a bad year without them. What I think is that the payment cap should apply per farm, not per family member, so the largest operations can't collect five times. That's a reform, not an abolition. SENATOR BAIRD: Would the senator support lowering the cap? SENATOR OKONJO: I'd look at it. I'd want to see the numbers for family farms first. SENATOR PELL: For the record, the audit office found that the top one percent of recipients received a large share of payments last year. state.truthledger_about: TruthLedger describes itself as 'independent citizen journalism'. Its pages carry no masthead, no named editor and no corrections policy.

The clerk added that members can request corrections to their own remarks only for transcription errors, not to change what was said, and that Senator Okonjo had requested no corrections for this session. The clerk declined to comment on the TruthLedger site itself, saying the office does not assess third-party publications. The full video of the session remains freely viewable on the Senate website.

desk_findings.fine: Harbour board decision confirms a $4,000 fine, paid in full within the appeal window. The article's figure was a typo in the reporter's notes.

desk_findings.other: The story's other facts, including the cleanup cost shortfall at three marinas, check out against board records. record.title: Sixteen weeks of supervised combined training versus usual care in adults with type 2 diabetes: the MOVE-T2 randomised trial
record.abstract: Background: Exercise is recommended for people with type 2 diabetes, but the effect of supervised combined aerobic and resistance training delivered in community gyms is uncertain. Methods: In this multicentre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial, we enrolled 212 adults aged 35 to 74 years with type 2 diabetes for at least one year and HbA1c between 7.0% and 10.0%. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) by a central web-based system to 16 weeks of supervised combined training three times per week or to usual care. Outcome assessors were masked to group allocation. The primary outcome was change in HbA1c at 16 weeks. Secondary outcomes included fasting plasma glucose, body weight, blood pressure and adverse events. Results: 198 participants (93%) completed the 16-week assessment. HbA1c decreased more in the training group than in the usual care group (mean difference -0.46 percentage points, 95% CI -0.68 to -0.24). Fasting glucose and body weight also improved. Four musculoskeletal adverse events occurred in the training group, none serious. Conclusions: Supervised combined training for 16 weeks improved glycaemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes. Trial registration: fictional registry TR-44120. Funding: National Diabetes Research Council (fictional).

record.title: SleepWell-U: a randomised trial of a digital CBT-I programme for students aged 16 to 24 with insomnia
record.abstract: Background: Insomnia is common among students and associated with poorer academic outcomes. Methods: Students aged 16 to 24 years with an Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) score of 10 or higher were recruited from three sixth-form colleges and two universities and randomised to SleepWell-U, a six-week fully automated programme covering sleep restriction, stimulus control, cognitive restructuring, relaxation and sleep hygiene, or to a waiting list. The primary outcome was ISI at 8 weeks. Results: 486 students were randomised; 41% were aged 16 or 17. At 8 weeks ISI was lower in the SleepWell-U group (adjusted difference -3.9 points). In a prespecified subgroup analysis restricted to participants aged 18 and over (n=287), the adjusted difference was -4.1 points (95% CI -5.0 to -3.2). Depressive symptoms (PHQ-9) also improved. Conclusions: Digital CBT-I reduced insomnia severity in students, including in adult participants analysed separately.

record.title: Early mobilisation after hip fracture surgery in a regional trauma unit: a controlled comparison
record.abstract: Objective: To compare an early mobilisation protocol (first out-of-bed session within 24 hours of surgery) with standard mobilisation (within 48 hours) after hip fracture surgery. Methods: Between March and November, consecutive patients aged 65 and over admitted for hip fracture surgery to a single trauma unit were allocated to early or standard mobilisation according to their day of admission: patients admitted on odd-numbered days received early mobilisation and those admitted on even-numbered days received standard care. Outcomes were independent walking at discharge, length of stay, and 30-day readmission. Results: 164 patients were allocated (early n=81, standard n=83). Independent walking at discharge was more frequent with early mobilisation. Length of stay was shorter by a median of two days. Readmission did not differ. Conclusions: Early mobilisation was associated with better functional outcomes.

Record REC-4410
Title: Proton pump inhibitor use and risk of community-acquired pneumonia in older adults: a population-based study

Abstract: Background: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are widely prescribed to older adults. Some studies suggest an association with pneumonia. Methods: Using a regional primary care database, we identified all adults aged 65 years and over with a first hospital admission for community-acquired pneumonia between two index years (cases). For each case, up to four controls without pneumonia were matched on age, sex, general practice and calendar time. Current PPI use was defined as a prescription within 30 days before the index date. Conditional logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios adjusted for comorbidities and co-medications. Results: We included 6,112 cases and 23,904 matched controls. Current PPI use was associated with increased odds of pneumonia (adjusted OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.19 to 1.44). The association was strongest in the first 30 days after starting treatment. Conclusions: Current PPI use is associated with a modest increase in pneumonia risk in older adults; residual confounding cannot be excluded.

record.methods_excerpt: Design. Two-arm parallel randomised trial in four hospitals. Participants. Adults discharged after an admission with a primary diagnosis of heart failure. Intervention. protocol_rules.R1: Include randomised controlled trials of iron supplementation in pregnant women with anaemia, reporting maternal haemoglobin.
protocol_rules.R2: Conference abstracts are excluded unless (a) a full publication of the same trial can be identified, in which case the full publication is used, or (b) the abstract itself reports extractable outcome data (a point estimate with a measure of variance) for a review outcome.
protocol_rules.R3: Where a trial registry record with posted results exists, it may be used in place of a full publication.

record.title: A randomised trial of a mindfulness app for anxiety in primary care
record.methods: Participants were recruited from 12 general practices. Adults aged 18 to 65 with a GAD-7 score of 8 or higher who owned a smartphone were eligible; people receiving psychological therapy were excluded. After baseline assessment, the research assistant opened the next envelope in a pile prepared by the trial statistician to reveal group allocation. Envelopes were not described as sealed or opaque. The allocation sequence was generated by computer in blocks of four. The intervention group received the Stillwater app (fictional) with eight weekly modules; the control group received a leaflet on anxiety and a list of local services. Participants and the research assistant who collected outcomes knew the allocation. The primary outcome was the GAD-7 score at 8 weeks, self-reported online. Secondary outcomes were PHQ-9 depression scores and app engagement (intervention group only).
record.results: Of 300 randomised participants, 186 completed the 8-week GAD-7 (intervention 81/150; control 105/150). Reasons for dropout were not reported. Analysis included completers only. GAD-7 scores were lower in the app group at 8 weeks. Median app engagement was three of eight modules.
record.registration: Registered retrospectively, after recruitment had finished.
record.funding: Funded by a university innovation grant. The app developer provided free licences and had no role in analysis, according to the authors.
record.discussion: The authors acknowledge that the completers-only analysis may overstate the effect if people who stopped using the app were those who did not benefit. They note that the leaflet control did not match the time and attention of the app, and that participants could not be blinded. They describe the trial as 'a pragmatic first evaluation' and call for a larger, prospectively registered trial with an attention-matched control and intention-to-treat analysis. No sensitivity analysis for missing data is reported, and the authors say the university's ethics committee did not require prospective registration at the time.

rob_guidance.allocation_concealment: Low risk only if allocation was concealed from those enrolling participants, e.g. central randomisation or sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes. If envelopes are used without these safeguards being described, rate as unclear or some concerns.
rob_guidance.missing_data: High risk if outcome data are missing for a substantial proportion, missingness differs between arms, and no reasons or sensitivity analyses are reported.
rob_guidance.selective_reporting: If registration was retrospective, the prespecified outcome cannot be confirmed; rate some concerns unless a protocol is available.

record.title: A randomised pilot trial of group music therapy for agitation in nursing home residents with dementia
record.abstract: Aims: To assess the feasibility of recruitment, retention and fidelity of a 10-week group music therapy programme, and to estimate the variability of agitation scores to inform the sample size of a definitive trial. Methods: Residents of four nursing homes were individually randomised to group music therapy or usual activities. Results: 64 of 92 eligible residents consented; 55 completed follow-up. Fidelity was high. Cohen-Mansfield Agitation Inventory scores were lower in the music therapy group, but the study was not powered to detect differences. Conclusions: A definitive trial is feasible.
